source.title: UPCORE: Utility-Preserving Coreset Selection for Balanced Unlearning
source.authors: Vaidehi Patil; Elias Stengel-Eskin; Mohit Bansal

page_placements.theme: Prompt variants leave more residual than direct queries, in settings or metrics E's verdicts did not count

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates whether unlearning results generalize to paraphrased and role-play jailbreak prompts, using its own topic-based setup and AUC evaluation rather than reproducing the cited attack studies.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates paraphrase and jailbreak variants after unlearning. It reports AUC values, but the attack tables have an apparent mismatch between the number of metric headings and values, so the values cannot safely be assigned to individual columns. The paper does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or whether unlearning reaches chance accuracy. Other results on utility, forget-set ROUGE, and transfer do not directly test those attack versions.
record.test_reason: The study proposes UPCORE, a forget-set selection method, and compares it with other selection baselines on a deletion-utility trade-off AUC. The paraphrase and role-play 'jailbreak' results (Tables 5/13) are reported only as AUC of (1−forget-variant ROUGE) against utility ROUGE across checkpoints. They never give forget-variant ROUGE or accuracy on its own, so they cannot show whether prompting restores forgotten knowledge (E). UPCORE also does not claim robustness to the recovery attacks in B–E, so F is not tested. A is not tested either: there are no near-chance accuracy targets or attack-recovery measurements; Table 3 reports forget ROUGE only on the original prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that UPCORE (pruning high-variance outliers from the forget set) improves the deletion-utility trade-off AUC over complete-set, random and D2-pruning baselines across GA, Refusal and NPO. They report that this advantage holds on paraphrased and role-play variants, and attribute it to positive transfer from the coreset. They do not claim robustness to knowledge-recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses coreset selection with gradient ascent, refusal, and NPO on topic-based factual QA data; the attack results here use gradient ascent on Counterfact. It does not test fine-tuning recovery, activation ablation, or quantization.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported attack evaluation is limited to paraphrase and role-play jailbreak variants; the study reports results for Gradient Ascent in these tables.

fits_no_version.finding: For Gradient Ascent on Counterfact, trade-off AUCs are lower on variant prompts than on the original forget prompts, with the same utility data. Complete-set Retain AUC is 0.488 on original prompts (Table 1), 0.417 on jailbreak and 0.357 on rephrase prompts (Table 13). This indirectly suggests deletion transfers incompletely to reworded prompts, but the AUC does not isolate forget ROUGE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deletion-utility trade-off AUC degrades when the forget set is probed with paraphrased or role-play variants (indirect, composite metric).

record.problems: The paraphrase and jailbreak tables show AUC summaries rather than direct recovery amounts, and the number of reported values does not match the apparent number of metric headings. Attack-table uncertainties are not stated. The attack evaluation is limited to one model, one unlearning method, and the reported prompt variants.
record.rows_left_out: Did not include standard trade-off tables, fixed-epoch forget/utility ROUGE results, or pruned-point transfer results because they do not directly measure the recovery attacks in versions B–F or targeted accuracy near chance in version A. The remaining attack-table results are retained in r1–r6 as flattened aggregates.

untested.parts: No near-chance accuracy target and no recovery attack measured directly. Forget ROUGE of about 0.017 (Table 3) is reported only on the original prompts.
No activation-direction ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis.
Paraphrase and role-play prompts are evaluated only inside a trade-off AUC. No forget-variant ROUGE is reported on its own. No other languages, adversarial jailbreaks, or in-context attacks.
UPCORE is a utility-preserving selection method and makes no claim to resist recovery attacks. It is not evaluated against fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or adversarial prompting.

missing.what: Forget-set ROUGE on paraphrase and jailbreak variants, separated from utility (the text says all metrics were evaluated on variants, but only AUC is shown)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's claimed column mismatch is an error: the tables have five metric columns and five values. The 'jailbreak' prompts are benign role-play rewordings generated by GPT-4o (the prompt says it is 'not asking for anything adversarial'). They are not optimized attacks. The setup is a single model (Llama-3.1-8B) with LoRA unlearning at layer 7.

versions.untested_parts: It reports forget-set ROUGE and utility metrics, but does not establish that targeted-knowledge accuracy reaches near chance while preserving general ability and resisting simple recovery attacks.
No fine-tuning recovery attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests paraphrase and one role-play jailbreak prompt style, but does not test other languages, in-context information, or report direct attack-induced recovery amounts.
Evaluates UPCORE with gradient ascent on paraphrase and role-play jailbreak variants only; it does not test resistance to fine-tuning, internal edits, or quantization attacks.

relation.reason: It applies gradient ascent, refusal and NPO unlearning, plus paraphrase/role-play evaluation, to test its own selection method. It does not measure knowledge recovery.

tranche.reason: UPCORE is a forget-set selection method. The jailbreak and rephrase results are given only as AUC of (1-ROUGE on the forget variant) against utility ROUGE across checkpoints. There is no pre-unlearning or recovery measure, so the study reports only its own method's trade-off and does not test the claim.

source_check.notes: The rows are composite deletion-utility AUCs, not recovery rates, so they bear on no claim version. The reader's alternative call (tests/T2) is not supported. Tables 5/13 cover only Gradient Ascent, comparing Complete, Random and UPCORE (no D2-pruning), with no error bars. The 'jailbreaks' are GPT-4o-generated role-play prompts. The setup is Llama-3.1-8B with rank-1 LoRA at layer 7, unlearning Counterfact topics.

statements.problem: None. For Gradient Ascent on Counterfact (Llama-3.1-8B), complete-set Retain AUC is 0.488 ± 0.015 on original forget prompts (Table 1, 3 seeds), 0.417 on jailbreak (Table 5/13) and 0.357 on rephrase (Table 13). The captions say 'with the same utility data'.
